title: File I/O Lifecycle: Write, Flush, and Read
description: Step-by-step trace of opening a file handle, streaming formatted student records to disk buffer, closing the stream descriptor, and reading back persisted data.

steps.explanation: Calling open('records.txt', 'w') requests a file descriptor from the OS in write mode. If records.txt does not exist, an empty file is created on storage.
f.write(...) writes 'RegNo: 101, Name: Arun\n' into Python's internal memory stream buffer. The OS prepares disk sectors for synchronization.
The second f.write(...) appends 'Marks: 94.5\n' into the stream buffer. Notice that write() does not add automatic newlines.
Calling f.close() flushes all remaining buffered bytes from RAM onto permanent secondary storage and releases the file descriptor back to the OS kernel.
Calling open('records.txt', 'r') opens the saved file in read-only mode. The file pointer cursor is initialized at offset byte 0 (start of file).
Calling f_read.read() traverses the whole file from start to EOF (End Of File) and loads the contents as a single Python string into variable 'content'.
The print(content) function writes the string to standard output (stdout), displaying the saved multi-line records on the terminal.
f_read.close() closes the reading stream. The file is cleanly preserved on disk for future program runs.
